questions.q: What did David do after defeating the Amalekites?
questions.a: David returned from defeating the Amalekites and remained in Ziklag for two days without receiving any news of the battle between the Philistines and Israelites.

questions.q: On the third day, who came to David from Saul’s camp?
questions.a: On the third day, a man with his clothes torn and with dirt on his head came to David.

questions.q: What did the young man say about Saul and Jonathan?
questions.a: The young man said that Saul and his son Jonathan were killed.

questions.q: Where did the young man say he found Saul?
questions.a: The young man said he was on Mount Gilboa, and Saul was there leaning on his spear.

questions.q: What did the young man say Saul asked him to do?
questions.a: The young man said Saul asked him to stand over him and kill him.

questions.q: Why did Saul ask the young Amalekite man to kill him?
questions.a: Saul asked the young Amalekite man to kill him because great agony had seized him, but his life was still in him.

questions.q: After the young man killed Saul, what did he take from Saul?
questions.a: The young man took the crown that was on Saul’s head and the band that was on his arm.

questions.q: What did David and his men do when they heard about the deaths of Saul and Jonathan?
questions.a: David and his men tore their clothes, and they mourned, wept, and fasted until evening.

questions.q: For whom else were David and his men mourning?
questions.a: David and his men also mourned for the people of Yahweh and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

questions.q: Why did David have the young Amalekite man killed?
questions.a: David had the young Amalekite man killed because the man’s own words testified that he had killed Yahweh’s anointed.

questions.q: Why did David have the young Amalekite man killed?
questions.a: David had the young Amalekite man killed because the man’s own words testified that he had killed Yahweh’s anointed.

questions.q: Where is the funeral song that David sang for Saul and Jonathan written?
questions.a: The song is written in the Book of Jashar.

questions.q: What was slain on Israel’s high places?
questions.a: The splendor of Israel was slain there.

questions.q: Why did David not want the news of the defeat proclaimed in Gath or Ashkelon?
questions.a: He did not want the daughters of the Philistines to rejoice or triumph.

questions.q: Where does the shield of the Saul, the mighty king, remain?
questions.a: The shield of the mighty king remains on ground on Mount Gilboa.

questions.q: What did Saul do for the daughters of Israel?
questions.a: He made Israel a safe and prosperous place in which they had beautiful scarlet clothes and expensive jewelry and gold ornaments to wear.

questions.q: How did David describe his love for Jonathan?
questions.a: David said Jonathan’s love for him was more wonderful than the love of women.

commentary.text: Tidings brought to David of the death of Saul.
The Amalekite is put to death.
David's lamentation for Saul and Jonathan.

Verses 1–10 The blow which opened David's way to the throne was given about the time he had been sorely distressed. Those who commit their concerns to the Lord, will quietly abide his will. It shows that he desired not Saul's death, and he was not impatient to come to the throne.

David was sincere in his mourning for Saul; and all with him humbled themselves under the hand of God, laid so heavily upon Israel by this defeat. The man who brought the tidings, David put to death, as a murderer of his prince. David herein did not do unjustly; the Amalekite confessed the crime. If he did as he said, he deserved to die for treason; and his lying to David, if indeed it were a lie, proved, as sooner or later that sin will prove, lying against himself. Hereby David showed himself zealous for public justice, without regard to his own private interest.

Kasheth, or “the bow,” probably was the title of this mournful, funeral song. David does not commend Saul for what he was not; and says nothing of his piety or goodness. Jonathan was a dutiful son, Saul an affectionate father, therefore dear to each other. David had reason to say, that Jonathan's love to him was wonderful. Next to the love between Christ and his people, that affection which springs form it, produces the strongest friendship. The trouble of the Lord's people, and triumphs of his enemies, will always grieve true believers, whatever advantages they may obtain by them.
